active_paradigms.idea: Replace runtime search with a static, independently certified 11-point elite configuration returned by numpy.asarray
active_paradigms.description: The evaluator has no hidden instance, no randomness requirement beyond determinism, and scores only the returned coordinates, so the highest-value deployment strategy is to do expensive discovery offline and return one stored configuration. The current program spends nearly all of its runtime repeatedly running differential evolution and SLSQP, yet fixes three points at the corners and can only retain the best basin encountered during that call. Run any exploratory research offline to build an archive of candidate configurations, including configurations where the three nominal corner points are allowed to move, then select the archive member with the largest recomputed minimum of all 165 normalized determinants. Store Cartesian coordinates with substantially more than double precision display precision, but recompute/check the actual float64 values that will be embedded. Before freezing the array, independently enumerate every triplet using the evaluator formula, identify all nearly active triples, and make a very small feasible inward adjustment only if needed to protect against decimal-rounding loss. The constructor itself should then only create and return that array, eliminating optimizer failure paths and making eval_time essentially negligible. This directly exploits the evaluator's static nature and is fundamentally stronger than trying to rediscover a difficult global optimum on every evaluation.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized first; this also maximizes combined_score, while reducing eval_time from repeated global optimization to an array construction.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not copy barycentric (u,v) values as though they were Cartesian coordinates; convert with x=u+v/2 and y=sqrt(3)v/2 before storing. Verify all 165 Cartesian areas after rounding and verify the three containment inequalities with a margin larger than 1e-6. A visually symmetric configuration is not sufficient: the limiting triples, including triples with no boundary vertex, determine the score.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.direct on an all-free barycentric parameterization, rather than assuming the three corners are members of the optimal set
active_paradigms.description: The current method is a stochastic differential-evolution search over only eight movable points because it permanently installs all three container vertices as points. That assumption is a major structural restriction: the evaluator never requires any point to be a vertex, and an optimum for a finite maximin set can trade a tiny loss on corner-related triangles for a larger gain in an interior bottleneck. Use scipy.optimize.direct as a deterministic partition-based global search over bounded variables (u_i,w_i), with v_i=(1-u_i)w_i, so every trial point is feasible without nonlinear constraints. Search all eleven points, or use a reduced geometric template in which only the previously forced corner points and their closest neighbors are released; preserve permutation handling by canonical ordering only after evaluation, not by invalid coordinate constraints. The objective should be the negative minimum absolute determinant over all 165 triples in barycentric coordinates, which exactly equals the evaluator's normalized area. DIRECT explores boxes rather than relying on random population basin coverage, so it can test whether the corner-fixed chirotope is genuinely competitive and identify a qualitatively different arrangement. Return the best feasible sample directly from this single global call; unlike the existing DE-plus-SLSQP pipeline, do not append a local polishing stage.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized by removing the unproven fixed-corner constraint and systematically covering orientation/placement basins; determinism is also improved relative to evolutionary search.
active_paradigms.cautions: DIRECT scales poorly in 22 unconstrained dimensions, so begin with a structured release of three to six coordinates around a strong stored seed/template rather than a completely unstructured full search if execution time is limited. Parameterize the simplex exactly instead of using penalties for outside points, since penalty discontinuities waste subdivisions. The minimum-area objective is nonsmooth at active-triple switches, so retain the best sampled point and do not expect the reported optimizer convergence flag alone to certify quality.

active_paradigms.idea: Polish a fixed active-contact geometry with scipy.optimize.root by solving equal-area contact equations rather than another epigraph minimization
active_paradigms.description: The current SLSQP stage freezes determinant signs and maximizes an epigraph, but it often terminates on a constrained nonsmooth face and is sensitive to its guessed active set; the previously failed one-shot minimize attempt is evidence that generic local NLP is not reliably selecting that face. For a strong candidate, explicitly inspect the 165 determinants and form its contact graph: include the triples at or extremely close to the minimum, plus the boundary equalities for points believed to lie on a side. Treat the common normalized area t and selected movable coordinates as unknowns, and use scipy.optimize.root to solve signed_det(triple)-t=0 for a square, independent subset of contact equations. Use an analytically constructed Jacobian of these determinant equations and start from the candidate, so this is a direct geometric equation solve rather than a second global optimization or hyperparameter fit. After the single root call, recompute every one of the 165 absolute determinants and accept the root only if it is inside the simplex and improves the true minimum; otherwise return the original deterministic seed. Repeat the contact-set design offline for several known chirotopes, then embed the best resulting seed/contact choice in the constructor. This targets the characteristic Heilbronn optimum structure, where many bottleneck triangles are expected to be exactly tied, and can recover precision that finite-tolerance SLSQP leaves on the table.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized through high-precision balancing of the active limiting triangles; it can be very fast at evaluation time because it solves a small deterministic system.
active_paradigms.cautions: The equation count must equal the number of free coordinate variables plus t after boundary coordinates are eliminated or constrained; use rank checks offline to avoid singular contact systems. Freeze determinant signs only from a nondegenerate seed and always validate all non-contact triples afterward, because solving equalities alone does not enforce their lower bounds. Root finding has no feasibility guarantees, so retain a prevalidated fallback array and reject any result with a determinant sign flip, an outside point, or a lower true minimum.

tried_paradigms.idea: One-shot signed-orientation epigraph solve with free boundary vertices using scipy.optimize.minimize
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses ten differential-evolution runs followed by a local SLSQP polish, fixes all three container vertices, and locks the signs of all 165 determinants only after each DE run. Its useful principle is the barycentric (u,v) coordinate system, where every determinant equals the evaluator's normalized area exactly. Replace that runtime pipeline by one direct SLSQP call on all 11 point coordinates plus epigraph variable t, initialized from a precomputed incumbent literal. Do not force points 0, 1, and 2 to be the three container vertices; constrain every point by u>=0, v>=0, and 1-u-v>=0, since the vertex assumption is a potentially material restriction. Obtain the signed determinant pattern from the incumbent and impose sign_ijk*det_ijk(u,v)>=t for every triple, together with the triangle constraints. Supply the analytic determinant Jacobian and an analytic objective gradient for -t, exactly as the present code partly does. This directly exploits the strong local geometry discovered by the current solution while allowing the optimizer to move or release a vertex if that increases the bottleneck. Use a fixed stored incumbent and return it if the one SLSQP result is infeasible or has a smaller true unsigned minimum.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; the formulation optimizes the evaluator's exact normalized determinant directly. It should also sharply reduce eval_time relative to ten DE searches and repeated polishing.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A sign pattern is valid only locally, so this is most effective when the stored initialization is already in the desired orientation cell. Validate the returned result using unsigned determinants over all 165 triples, not merely the signed constraints. Give boundary constraints for every point, and leave a small numerical margin before Cartesian conversion to avoid violating the evaluator's 1e-6 containment tolerance.

tried_paradigms.idea: Discrete threshold-feasibility construction on a triangular lattice with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: Use a fundamentally different combinatorial certificate approach rather than searching continuous coordinates at evaluation time. Build a fixed candidate set in barycentric coordinates from a sufficiently fine triangular lattice, optionally augmented by a curated set of known good non-lattice rational locations, all of which are exactly inside u+v<=1. Choose a target normalized area slightly above the current approximately 0.793364 times benchmark, or directly test the benchmark threshold if the candidate set is rich enough. For every candidate triple whose absolute determinant is below that target, add the binary conflict inequality x_i+x_j+x_k<=2, and add the cardinality equality sum_i x_i=11. Make one scipy.optimize.milp call with integrality one and zero objective, or with a small deterministic secondary linear objective to select a reproducible feasible set. A feasible solution proves that its selected 11 points meet the threshold on the chosen candidate set, and those points can be returned directly without any continuous post-processing. This changes the difficult nonconvex area problem into a set-packing-style feasibility problem and explores orientation patterns that the current sign-locked local polish may never visit. Once an especially good discrete arrangement has been found during development, freeze its coordinates as literals in the submitted constructor for near-zero evaluation time.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly targets min_area_normalized through forbidden low-area triples, with a route to a deterministic, constant-time final returned arrangement. It trades coordinate resolution and MILP size against achievable area.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The threshold must be expressed in barycentric determinant units, which are already normalized area units; do not introduce the Cartesian factor sqrt(3)/2. A full dense lattice creates O(N^3) triples, so only generate conflicts below the target and use a deliberately bounded candidate pool. If MILP reports infeasible or times out, return a validated fixed fallback rather than the fractional/undefined solution. This is a construction method; no continuous polish should be applied if maintaining the single-call design.

tried_paradigms.idea: Orientation-unrestricted global basin search over all movable points with scipy.optimize.dual_annealing
tried_paradigms.description: The main limitation of the current program is that its local phase cannot cross a zero-determinant orientation wall, while its global phase spends most of its work in a parameterization that permanently fixes the three corners. Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing once on all 22 unconstrained real parameters, mapping each pair deterministically into the simplex by u=sigmoid(a) and v=(1-u)*sigmoid(b). This guarantees every proposed point lies inside the equilateral triangle without penalty constraints, and unlike the current local epigraph solve the objective remains the true negative minimum of the absolute values of all 165 determinants. Set fixed bounds such as [-28,28] for each latent coordinate so the search can effectively place points on any boundary while avoiding floating-point overflow. Seed the annealer deterministically and initialize or bias its first visit around a strong stored configuration transformed into latent variables. Use a sufficiently large visit parameter and iteration budget because determinant-sign changes are precisely the transitions that must be explored. Return the best feasible mapped state tracked by the objective, not an optimizer's potentially unavailable local-search result. This is particularly useful as an offline discovery method for a new orientation basin; after discovery, hard-code the resulting coordinates for the final fast constructor.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized through the exact nonsmooth evaluator objective while removing both the fixed-corner assumption and fixed-orientation-cell restriction. Runtime is worse during discovery but becomes negligible if the discovered arrangement is frozen.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Dual annealing is not competitive as a per-evaluation search if the evaluator has a tight wall-clock limit; use it to discover a literal candidate, then submit the literal. The sigmoid map only approaches exact boundaries, so use a large but safe latent bound and verify the final unsigned minimum in double precision. Point-label permutations create many equivalent states, so canonicalizing the initial literal can improve reproducibility, but do not sort dynamically in the objective because it creates artificial discontinuities.

tried_paradigms.idea: Run one global constrained differential-evolution epigraph search with all 11 points movable, rather than fixing the three container vertices and then freezing an orientation basin.
tried_paradigms.description: The current program maps barycentric coordinates correctly, and its determinant is exactly the evaluator's normalized area, which is a major strength. It then fixes three points at the corners, uses differential evolution only over the other eight, and applies SLSQP after fixing every determinant sign from the DE endpoint. This can miss better configurations because neither the inclusion of all three corners nor the discovered oriented-matroid/sign pattern is guaranteed globally optimal. Use one scipy.optimize.differential_evolution call over 22 barycentric variables plus an epigraph variable t, with every point represented by two bounded variables transformed to u>=0, v>=0, u+v<=1. Make the objective -t and use a scipy.optimize.NonlinearConstraint returning abs(det_ijk)-t for all 165 triples, so the objective exactly matches the evaluator rather than relying on a minimum-area objective with nondifferentiable basin behavior. Remove only rigid Euclidean symmetries safely, for example constrain one selected point to the base edge and use a canonical lexicographic ordering convention if it is encoded without excluding solutions. Use a deterministic seed, a large population, Sobol initialization, and workers=1 for reproducibility. Return the feasible endpoint directly after independently recomputing the minimum determinant and, if numerical constraint tolerance is marginal, decrease t only for validation rather than moving the coordinates.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize min_area_normalized; this removes the current fixed-corner and fixed-sign restrictions, both of which can cap the score below the benchmark.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not use Cartesian box bounds without containment constraints: the evaluator rejects even tiny genuinely infeasible violations beyond 1e-6. DE constrained feasibility can be sparse, so barycentric feasibility should be built into the transform and the nonlinear constraints should only represent triangle-area epigraph inequalities. The returned score must be recomputed from coordinates, not trusted from result.fun or t.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use SHGO on a low-dimensional, explicitly enumerated geometric order-type family to obtain a deterministic global basin certificate rather than stochastic sampling of 16 dimensions.
tried_paradigms.description: The current method is effective because the signed-area epigraph becomes smooth once an orientation pattern is selected, but its DE stage has no systematic mechanism to cover the relevant patterns. Construct a compact family from the expected extremal geometry: boundary points parameterized by one edge coordinate, reflection-paired interior points parameterized in barycentric coordinates, and any required symmetry-axis points parameterized by one coordinate. For each genuinely distinct dihedral/reflection order type chosen offline, formulate t and all coordinates as variables, use signed determinant inequalities for that family, and call scipy.optimize.shgo once with the simplicial sampling method and those nonlinear constraints. The signed constraints are valid only after ensuring the proposed order type; they eliminate the absolute-value discontinuity that hinders global methods. SHGO's sampling and local minimization can identify multiple separated feasible basins deterministically, unlike the current set of arbitrarily selected DE seeds. Select the single best family by its verified actual absolute minimum area, then hard-code that resulting arrangement in the submitted constructor so evaluation time is negligible. This strategy is structurally different from searching arbitrary point clouds: it exploits the fact that extremal Heilbronn layouts commonly have many active equal-area triples and boundary contacts.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Increase min_area_normalized through systematic coverage of plausible extremal order types; after offline discovery, minimize eval_time by returning fixed coordinates.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not impose full threefold rotational symmetry merely because the container is equilateral: 11 is not naturally decomposed into only size-three orbits, and an unjustified symmetry can rule out the optimum. Every proposed family must leave enough degrees of freedom for unequal boundary spacings and must be scored using all 165 absolute determinants, including triples not used as constraints. SHGO is unsuitable for the unrestricted 22-dimensional formulation, so dimensional reduction must be a justified geometric hypothesis rather than arbitrary coordinate fixing.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a binary grid/order-selection MILP to discover high-area combinatorial layouts, replacing continuous orientation-basin search with a forbidden-small-triangle packing formulation.
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator only cares about the smallest of 165 triangle areas, so for a fixed target threshold the problem can be converted into a discrete feasibility problem on a dense triangular candidate grid. Generate a deterministic candidate set in barycentric coordinates, preferably a nonuniform grid enriched near edges and near coordinates seen in good continuous layouts. For every candidate triple whose normalized determinant is below a chosen area level, add the linear forbidden-triple inequality x_i+x_j+x_k<=2; choosing 11 grid sites then guarantees no selected grid triangle is below that level. Encode several ordered area levels using binary level-selection variables and activate the corresponding forbidden-triple inequalities, then make one scipy.optimize.milp call maximize the selected level while requiring sum_i x_i=11. This is fundamentally different from the current continuous DE-plus-SLSQP pipeline: it searches the combinatorial incidence structure and can expose an order type that the current ten stochastic seeds never enter. Use the best selected grid arrangement as the final hard-coded answer if it already beats the incumbent, or use it only offline to identify a promising active-triple graph and derive a static continuous layout before submission. Evaluate every selected solution with the exact floating-point determinant formula, not grid cell estimates.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primarily improve min_area_normalized by finding globally separated point-set combinatorics; a hard-coded selected layout gives essentially zero runtime cost.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A uniform grid that is too coarse has a strict discretization ceiling and may never beat 0.029, while a very dense grid creates O(M^3) forbidden triples. Build the fixed candidate set so only triples plausibly below the highest relevant thresholds are enumerated, and include boundary candidates because the current solution's corner assumption should be tested rather than blindly retained. MILP feasibility proves a threshold only on the candidate grid, not for the continuous problem, so it is a discovery/certification tool and the final coordinates still need exact evaluator validation.
